title: Context, models, memory and knowledge
text:
**CX-01 — One context fabric.** `gen_ui_context` resolves device, model and runtime profiles plus measured session envelope into an effective budget. The builder owns ordering, truncation, tool shortlisting, retrieval and escalation. UI adapters load profiles and display decisions; they do not duplicate budget arithmetic. A model's advertised context length is not its measured reliable retrieval capacity.

**CX-02 — Budget invariant.** System, tool schemas, history, memories, knowledge, output reserve, reasoning reserve and margin must fit the effective ceiling. Exact tokenizer counts are preferred; heuristic estimates carry an explicit wider margin and telemetry. Context presets in the retained source are initial targets. Validate their arithmetic on every turn, especially when reasoning is enabled, rather than assuming source tables are internally additive. Thermal pressure or sustained latency reduces the local budget and offers an explicit handoff choice.

**CX-03 — Strategies.** Preserve sliding window, truncate-middle with counted omission marker, progressive summary, hierarchical short/mid/long-term memory, and pre-compact triggers. Never split a tool call from its result. Summaries store covered turn IDs and provenance. If summarization fails or is thermally disallowed, fall back visibly to sliding window for that turn. Fact extraction is opt-in and writes through the governed memory store rather than a hidden second memory.

**CX-04 — Retrieval.** Preserve atomic short notes, semantic boundary chunking, recursive overlap, and parent-child retrieval. Chunks have stable document/ordinal IDs, source spans, token estimates and ingestion provenance; document replacement is transactional. Separate memory and knowledge budgets prevent a large document from starving explicit personal memory. Fuse eligible vector/BM25/graph lanes, apply bounded diversity/recency ranking and deterministic placement. A cross-encoder is a measured follow-up, not a default mobile burden.

**CX-05 — Model resolution.** Global role slots, agent/Hand pins, deployment-target configuration and conversation overrides resolve to a permitted provider/model with required capabilities. Preserve `provider::model` identity, embedding model/dimension stamps, re-embedding migrations, explicit cloud consent and local-only usage-based suggestions. Remote fallback is a proposal, never a silent privacy downgrade. A model unavailable on the current device produces an honest state with alternative placement choices.

**CX-06 — Acquisition.** Retain curated catalog provenance, license gating, user-chosen model imports, resumable downloads, content integrity, available storage checks, hardware/memory probes, and post-download validation. Source engine/model combinations are lane-specific and historically dated. Certify model load, tokenizer/template correctness, bounded generation, tool/structured output semantics and physical-device resource behavior against actual artifacts. A successful download is not a successful local inference deployment.

**CX-07 — Knowledge base.** Preserve source-linked knowledge/wikis, incremental ingestion, link/provenance graphs, stale-source detection, index rebuilds and export. Derived summaries do not overwrite originals or acquire higher authority than their sources. Deletion propagates through eligible indexes and derived artifacts with an inspectable receipt; it cannot recall previously disclosed text from another participant or provider.

**CX-08 — Capture and tools.** Ask Image, Audio Scribe, Prompt Lab and Skills remain first-class workflows. Vision/OCR/document extraction preserve attachments and source spans; Audio Scribe keeps recording, transcription, speaker labels and summaries distinct; Prompt Lab supports ephemeral single-turn templates and model comparison; Skills distinguish atomic tools from packaged practices with instructions and policy proposals. MCP is an adapter at the edge, not a bypass around grants or budgets.

S07-002 · 1. Executive summary

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1. Executive summary

KnowMe's promise — "it knows the user" — is delivered through three inputs (memories, dropped-note RAG, tools) fed to models whose real capacity varies by two orders of magnitude across deployment targets: a Q4_K_M Qwen3.5-4B on a Galaxy S25 Ultra is not a cloud frontier model, and pretending otherwise produces an app that works in demos and fails in pockets. Today, context assembly is implicit and scattered: gen_ui_agent::chat builds message lists ad hoc, gen_ui_db_graph retrieves without budget awareness, tool schemas are injected wholesale, and nothing enforces the token arithmetic that on-device models require.

This specification defines one context fabric: a gen_ui_context crate in the shared Rust core that owns (a) a three-layer capabilities model (device / model / runtime) resolved into an EffectiveBudgetPlan, (b) a deterministic ContextBuilder pipeline that fills that plan in a fixed order, (c) the four context-management strategies from the Cherry Studio fork, ported natively (sliding window, truncate-middle, progressive summarization, hierarchical memory) plus the agent pre-compact trigger, (d) a chunking subsystem for dropped documents, and (e) a retrieval/re-ranking pipeline (existing RRF → MMR diversity → recency decay → placement policy). Every surface — Flutter mobile, Tauri desktop, web/WASM, Axum cloud — consumes the same crate through the same trait seams already used for InferenceProvider; platforms differ only in the capability profile they load, never in pipeline logic.

The design thesis is the same as the rest of the Fabric: architectural correctness over feature count. The model plans nothing about its own context; the harness owns budgets, ordering, truncation, and escalation as deterministic Rust. This is not a stylistic preference — the research base (§3) shows small on-device models measurably cannot self-manage tool memory, long contexts, or multi-step state, and that structured subsystems recover most of the gap.

S07-003 · 2. Scope, goals, non-goals

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2. Scope, goals, non-goals

Goals

  1. A single capability + budget abstraction controlling: system prompt size, history window, memory injection count/tokens, knowledge-base retrieval count/tokens, tool shortlist size, tool-schema tokens, output reserve, thinking reserve, re-ranking configuration — on every platform.
  2. Port the four fork strategies as first-class Rust implementations with the fork's layered override model (global → assistant/agent → topic/session).
  3. Chunking for dropped notes/documents with provenance, integrated with the existing gen_ui_db_graph ingest path without breaking atomic short notes.
  4. Deterministic, testable assembly: same inputs + same profile ⇒ same prompt, byte-for-byte, on every platform.
  5. Telemetry parity with the fork (tokensBefore/After/Saved, alteration summary) surfaced on the AG-UI stream.

Non-goals (v1)

  • Cross-encoder re-ranking (deferred behind a measurement gate, §10.4).
  • Model fine-tuning / LoRA for tool calling (separate initiative; §3.4 notes when it becomes the higher-leverage move).
  • Changing the embedding model or EMBED_DIM (stays 384 / all-MiniLM-L6-v2).
  • Prompt-content authoring (skills/personas). This spec governs assembly and budgets, not what the system prompt says.

S07-004 · 3. Research foundation (condensed, with sources)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3. Research foundation (condensed, with sources)

Findings gathered across this design session; each shaped a specific mechanism below. Full citations in §16.

3.1 Effective context ≪ nominal context. Qwen3.5-4B and -9B share an identical 32-layer hybrid layout — 8 × (3 × Gated DeltaNet → 1 × Gated Attention), full_attention_interval: 4 — so both have exactly 8 full-attention "precision checkpoints"; the difference is width (2560 vs 4096 hidden), not checkpoint density. GDN layers compress history into fixed-size recurrent state; precise recall depends on the 8 full-attention layers. Nominal 262K is a training capability, not a usable retrieval window. Consequence: 8K operating ceiling, 16K only behind an explicit degraded-mode flag; reliable RAG budget is low thousands of tokens (§7 tables).

3.2 Quantization compounds with context length. 8-bit ≈ −0.8% on long-context suites; 4-bit methods lose up to 59% worst-case, damage growing past 8K; K-quants are gentler than GPTQ/BNB-nf4 but Q4_K_M is still 4-bit. The GDN-recurrent-state × 4-bit interaction is uncharacterized in the literature — an explicit empirical risk. Consequence: needle-in-haystack smoke test against our actual GGUFs is a Phase 0 gate, not an afterthought.

3.3 Position matters ("lost in the middle"). Small models retrieve worst at 20–70% depth. Consequence: the placement policy (§10.3): best hit last (adjacent to the query), second-best first, middle treated as distractor space.

3.4 Agentic limits. Success ∝ (1−p)^m — 99% per-step accuracy is 36.6% at 100 steps; per-step accuracy itself degrades with step count (self-conditioning). Deviations on mutating actions reduce success odds by up to 92–96%; read-only deviations barely matter (SABER). Tool-selection accuracy degrades past ~20–25 exposed tools; Anthropic measured 58 tools ≈ 55K tokens. Two-stage retrieve-then-load gives ~6× system-prompt reduction and 10–25× context-growth reduction (TinyAgent/ToolRAG lineage). Small models cannot self-manage tool memory (MemTool); structured subsystems close the gap (fastWorkflow). Consequence: max 3–4 autonomous steps before checkpoint, individual gates on all mutating actions, 5–8 tool shortlist ceiling, harness owns planning. A purpose-LoRA over our real schemas becomes the better investment only after a tool cluster stabilizes — not before.

3.5 Thermal envelope is a budget dimension. Sustained inference: iPhone −41.5% throughput plateau (Hot state by ~iteration 17); S25-class GPU cliffs 680→231 MHz at 78.3 °C; shell >42 °C in 100 s at peak; dense on-device RAG prefill has exceeded 14 s TTFT in published deployments. Consequence: the SessionEnvelope (§6.4) tracks cumulative inference and degrades or hands off to cloud; RAG budgets also bound prefill latency, not just recall.

3.6 Structured output. Grammar-constrained decoding (llguidance, already a declared-but-unwired feature of our vendored llama-cpp-2) makes malformed JSON structurally impossible; it fixes shape, not semantics. Consequence: wire llama-cpp-2/llguidance into both mobile composite features; keep in-prompt tool descriptions to name + one line; compile grammars once per session; temp 0.0–0.2 on structured turns; post-parse semantic validation; 1–2 capped repair retries then fail closed.

4. Current-state review

S07-006 · 4.1 know-me-system (Rust workspace)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.1 know-me-system (Rust workspace)

What exists and is kept:

  • InferenceProvider trait seam (gen_ui_inference): engines behind a trait; Android = LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 E2B through the Rust boundary, iOS retains the existing llama.cpp/Qwen lane until re-certification, desktop has its own local engine lanes. The context fabric slots in as a sibling seam, not inside any engine.
  • Hybrid retrieval (gen_ui_db_graph): SurrealDB search::rrf fuses vector + BM25 lanes; rrf.rs fuses the RELATE graph-hop lane (k=60, limit=20) with an explicitly documented constraint — RRF only for lanes that can agree; disjoint-ordered lanes score by hop distance. Kept as-is; the new pipeline wraps it (§10).
  • Embedder trait (embed.rs): 384-dim, model-provenance check, batch API, spawn_blocking discipline. Chunking reuses it unchanged.
  • Atomic note ingest (corpus.rs/store.rs): memory_ingest embeds each note whole; idempotent stable ids. Correct for short notes; there is no document chunking anywhere — the gap §9 fills.
  • Streaming chat loop (gen_ui_agent::chat): OpenAI-shaped streaming with tool-call accumulation across chunks. It currently assembles context inline; after this spec it requests an assembled context from the builder.

Gaps this spec closes: no capability profiles; no budget arithmetic anywhere; no chunking; no MMR/recency re-ranking; no history strategies; Android tool calling now targets LiteRT-LM constrained decoding/manual tools rather than llama.cpp llguidance; no context telemetry.

S07-008 · 5. Architecture

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5. Architecture

S07-009 · 5.1 Crate placement

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.1 Crate placement

New workspace crate gen_ui_context (Rust, no engine deps, no_std-clean core not required but wasm32-clean is):

gen_ui_types ──► gen_ui_context ──► consumed by: gen_ui_agent, gen_ui_host,
                     │                gen_ui_server_axum, gen_ui_ffi,
                     │                gen_ui_wasm, tauri-plugin-gen-ui
                     ├── depends on: gen_ui_db_graph (retrieval traits only)
                     └── never depends on: gen_ui_inference engines

Capability inversion holds: gen_ui_context knows about budgets and retrieval capabilities through traits; it never links an inference engine, and no engine crate links it. gen_ui_agent asks the builder for an AssembledContext; the builder asks injected providers (history store, memory store, KB store, tool registry, token estimator) for slices. Compile-time dependency direction is the guarantee, per the standing Fabric invariant.

S07-021 · 7.2 Derivation rules

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7.2 Derivation rules

Given C = context_ceiling after safety margin:

  1. output_reserve and thinking_reserve come off the top (never squeezed).
  2. system_prompt_max + tool_schema_max are fixed by tier.
  3. history_max fixed by tier; strategy (§8) keeps history inside it.
  4. memory_max + knowledge_max = remainder, split by tier ratio (default 30/70 — dropped notes are the larger corpus; memories are short).
  5. Invariant checked at resolve time: Σ slices + margin ≤ C — violation is a config error, not a runtime clamp.

8.2 SlidingWindow

Token-budget-first (the fork's "dynamic" mode becomes the primary mode): admit turns newest→oldest until history_max or max_history_messages is hit; maxMessages remains as an optional cap for fork parity. Never splits a turn; never separates a tool call from its result (a constraint the fork handles upstream via filters — here it is a builder invariant).

8.3 TruncateMiddle

S07-028 · 8.4 Summarize (progressive)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.4 Summarize (progressive)

Real implementation, not fallback. Trigger: history over history_max AND turn count ≥ summarize_threshold (6). The oldest overflow block is summarized into ≤ summary_max_tokens (500) by a summarizer route: on-device it reuses the loaded model with a short constrained prompt at temp 0.2 (one extra inference — the SessionEnvelope charges it); cloud/desktop may route to a designated small model (fork's summarizationModelId). SummaryRecord persists (SurrealDB, §11.3) with the covered turn-ids so re-summarization is incremental — fork's summarizedMessageIds parity. Failure mode honored: if the summarizer call fails or the envelope forbids the extra inference, degrade to SlidingWindow for this turn and record it in telemetry; never block the user's message on a summary.

S07-029 · 8.5 Hierarchical (three-tier) — the KnowMe-native strategy

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.5 Hierarchical (three-tier) — the KnowMe-native strategy

Short-term: last short_term_turns (5) verbatim. Mid-term: rolling summary inside mid_term_summary_tokens (2000 desktop/cloud; clamped to the history slice on mobile). Long-term: extracted durable facts within long_term_facts_tokens (500). The KnowMe twist: long-term facts are not a parallel store — extraction writes them through the existing memory ingest (gen_ui_db_graph::memory_ingest, kind "fact", provenance = session id), so hierarchical memory and user memories converge on one governed store and facts become retrievable by the same RRF pipeline in future sessions. This is the mechanism that makes "it knows the user" compound over time. Extraction is opt-in per assistant and surfaced in the UI (sovereignty: users see what was written and can delete it; deletion respects the standing memory-removal path).

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

8.6 PreCompactPolicy (agent/cloud lane)

Fork parity: cache the prior turn's total-token usage; when it exceeds compact_trigger_tokens, run a compaction step (strategy-mediated summarize) before dispatching the next user message. On-device this maps to "force-summarize now"; on cloud SDK sessions it maps to the provider compact primitive where one exists.

S07-035 · 10. Retrieval & re-ranking pipeline

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10. Retrieval & re-ranking pipeline

S07-036 · 10.1 Stages

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.1 Stages

query ──► lanes (vector | BM25 | graph-hop)      [existing gen_ui_db_graph]
      ──► RRF fuse (k=60, limit=20)              [existing, unchanged]
      ──► MMR diversity pass (λ default 0.7)     [new — embedding math only]
      ──► recency boost: score × exp(−λr·age_d)  [new — λr per corpus kind]
      ──► truncate to max_kb_retrievals / max_memory_items
      ──► optional parent widening (§9.3)
      ──► placement (§10.3)

MMR uses the vectors already fetched for the RRF candidates — zero extra model calls, bounded O(k²) at k ≤ 20. Recency defaults: memories λr = 0.01/day (gentle), facts 0.005, chunks 0 unless the doc kind opts in. Both passes are pure functions with property tests.

S07-037 · 10.2 Memory vs knowledge lanes

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.2 Memory vs knowledge lanes

Memories and knowledge chunks are retrieved as separate pipeline runs against separate ledger slices (memory_max / knowledge_max). One shared run would let a large dropped document starve the user's explicit memories — the exact inversion of the product promise.

S07-038 · 10.3 PlacementPolicy

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.3 PlacementPolicy

Per §3.3: rank-1 item is placed last in its section (adjacent to the user query); rank-2 first; remaining ranks fill the middle. Sections order: system → tools → long-term facts → history → memories → knowledge → query. Placement is deterministic and covered by golden tests: same inputs, same bytes.

S07-039 · 10.4 Cross-encoder gate (deferred)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

10.4 Cross-encoder gate (deferred)

Add a reranker model only if, after MMR+recency ship, retrieval precision is still the measured bottleneck (eval set: ≥50 real query/expected-note pairs; precision@3 target 0.8). If added: runs over RRF top-15–20 only, desktop/cloud first; mobile only if the envelope affords it. Until that gate, the extra forward passes buy less than they cost on-device.

S07-045 · 13. Failure scenarios & trade-offs (what hurts)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

13. Failure scenarios & trade-offs (what hurts)

Per standing discipline, the scenarios that hurt this design, named:

  1. Token-estimation drift. chars/4 on Qwen3.5's 248K vocab can misestimate by 20–30% on code/multilingual text; even the exact tokenizer path costs an FFI round-trip per slice. Mitigation is the widened margin + estimator telemetry, but a systematic underestimate still means silent quality loss near the ceiling. Residual risk: medium until P0-2 measures real drift.
  2. Summarization on-device is an extra inference. It competes with the thermal envelope and adds latency exactly when conversations are longest. The degrade-to-sliding-window path caps the damage but means the summarize strategy silently behaves like sliding window on hot devices — users may perceive memory loss. Telemetry makes it visible; it does not make it free.
  3. GDN × Q4 interaction is uncharacterized. If the P0-3 needle test shows retrieval breaking below 8K on either GGUF, every tier table in §7.3 shrinks and the product's on-device RAG story narrows. Probability subjectively 20–35%; impact contained because trusted_context is a data field, not a constant.
  4. Two token vocabularies of truth. Fork-era chats managed by chars/4 and fabric-era chats managed by exact counts will window differently; users migrating desktop→mobile may see different history depth. Accepted; documented in release notes rather than papered over.
  5. Preset ossification. Hardcoded tier numbers rot as models/devices change. Mitigation: presets are data files versioned with the app + overridable server-side for cloud tier; the needle test is rerun per new GGUF as a release gate.
  6. The scenario that hurts Prometheus: a competitor ships "just use the cloud" with a 200K window and no budget UX, and it feels smarter on day one. Our counter is compounding personal memory (§8.5) + sovereignty + consistency — but that is a bet on retention economics, not an immediate demo win, and it should be stated as such to stakeholders.

Phase 3 — Chunking + retrieval upgrades (1.5–2 wks, 75%) Chunk router/strategies, SurrealDB schema, MMR + recency passes, placement, memory/knowledge slice separation, citation provenance to ContentBlock. Exit: precision@3 eval harness exists with baseline numbers recorded.

Phase 4 — Platform adapters (1–2 wks, 70%) FFI surface (flutter_rust_bridge), Tauri command, wasm build, Axum middleware; preset loading + envelope probes per platform. Exit: same golden assembly bytes on all four targets in CI.

Phase 5 — Field hardening (1–1.5 wks, 60%) Context inspector UI hook-up, degraded-mode UX, PreCompactPolicy on cloud lane, telemetry ring bounds, release-gate automation for P0-3 reruns.

S25-002 · 1. What Cherry Studio gets right (and what we adopt)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1. What Cherry Studio gets right (and what we adopt)

From the Cherry Studio default-models docs, chat docs, and the model-configuration internals:

  1. Role-slot defaults, not one global model. Separate defaults for the default assistant model, a fast model for background chores (topic naming, keyword extraction), and a translation model — "the models used by the behind-the-scenes helpers," explicitly distinct from the chat model. Adopt, with more roles (§3).
  2. Assistant = role, Topic = conversation with that role. The assistant pins the system prompt, model, and sampling params; topics inherit; any topic can override; @-mention temporarily borrows another model for one reply while keeping context; an auto-reset policy decides whether new topics revert to the assistant's model or inherit the last override. Adopt all four behaviors verbatim (§4).
  3. Deterministic model identity: providerId::modelId. One key format everywhere (their user_model table), with per-model capabilities, userOverrides, and orderKey. Adopt — it is exactly what our entity graph and OFP sync want (§2).
  4. Capability tags with a resolution precedence. vision / function-calling / reasoning / embedding / rerank per model; resolved as registry-force → user overrides → registry add/remove, so user removals survive registry updates. Adopt precedence unchanged (§2.3).
  5. Provider-specific settings are schema, not special-cased UI (Azure api-version, Vertex project, custom OpenAI-compatible base URLs). Adopt via our settings-schema renderer (§2.2) — one generic form engine, per-provider schemas.

Where we must diverge: Cherry Studio is a single-machine app. KnowMe's config must survive multiple devices with different local capabilities plus shared peers — that changes identity, resolution, and sync (§5).

{

Two provider kinds are KnowMe-specific and auto-registered, never hand-configured:

  • bossfang — one provider per connected instance from Settings → Instances, created/removed with the instance itself. Its model list is served by the peer (the cyan remote rows in the moodboard). Health = OFP reachability.

Cloud kinds route through liter-llm in UAR — the vendored submodule (rust/vendor/universal-agent-runtime v1.0.0) carries a 269-provider catalog as discovery data (a catalog entry is not execution certification; provider access stays capability- and health-gated) — but are presented as first-class providers with their own rows, keys, and health checks. Every provider row: status dot · label · base host · kind pill · "Check" button (connectivity + auth + a 1-token echo), matching the moodboard Providers tab.

S25-011 · 4.3 Resolution order (the whole system in six lines)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

4.3 Resolution order (the whole system in six lines)

message-level  @mention            (one reply)
  → conversation override          (sticky, this topic)
    → assistant/Hand pin           (+ params; Hands: scoped to deployment target)
      → role slot                  (chat.default / agent.default / …)
        → device recommendation    (local-models §10, if the slot is unset)

Every level may be unset; the effective choice always renders its source. One hard rule from the sovereignty posture: resolution never escalates locality on its own — a chain that resolves to a local model may fall back to a peer, but falling back to a cloud provider requires an existing Cedar grant for that provider, or a prompt.

S25-012 · 5. Multi-device semantics (where we go beyond Cherry Studio)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5. Multi-device semantics (where we go beyond Cherry Studio)

A pinned local-engine model may not exist on the next device. Resolution therefore has a placement walk when the bound ref is unavailable here:

  1. Same model_id on a reachable bossfang provider → use it (chip shows cyan remote);
  2. Same catalog equivalence class locally (the signed catalog groups e.g. Qwen3 {4B, 8B, 14B} as tier-variants of one family; pick the device-appropriate tier and label it "device equivalent");
  3. Offer: download it here (jumps into the local-models §2 flow) / pick another / use peer.

Sync scopes (per the extensibility-spec settings model): role slots and assistant pins are user-scoped (CRDT-synced); the placement of local-engine refs and anything bound to device hardware is device-scoped; provider auth is secret (keychain, never CRDT — each device holds its own copy; BossFang instances may hold shared keys in Flint Vault). Conversation overrides travel with the conversation entity through normal OFP sync, and the placement walk re-runs on whatever device opens it.

S25-013 · 6. Embedding models — per-index bindings, not a global knob

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6. Embedding models — per-index bindings, not a global knob

The embedding.default slot only seeds creation flows. The binding that matters lives on the index, because vectors are only comparable within one model+dim (local-models §11):

// stamped on every KB / karpathy wiki / log index / loop memory at creation
{
  "index_id": "kb-client-acme",
  "embedding": { "model_ref": "prov-local::embeddinggemma-300m", "dim": 256 },
  "rerank":    { "model_ref": null },
  "chunking":  { "strategy": "semantic", "target_tokens": 480, "overlap": 64 },
  "created_at": "…"
}
  • Immutable after creation except through an explicit re-embed migration: a visible job (progress, cancellable, old index kept until the new one completes) — the honest version of what most tools hide. Cherry Studio binds the embedding model at KB creation for the same reason; we make the migration path first-class instead of impossible.
  • Creation wizard: defaults from embedding.default, shows dim choice with the tradeoff stated ("256-dim: ~3× smaller/faster, slight recall cost — recommended on this device"), warns when the chosen model can't run on devices that sync this index ("your phone can embed queries with EmbeddingGemma but not BGE-M3 — queries will route to a peer").
  • Karpathy wikis / logs / loops (the karpathy-progress-memory artifacts): each gets the same binding block. Their maintenance passes (summarize, distill, link) draw from utility.fast; their retrieval uses the index's own embedding binding; loops that grade/reflect may pin a reasoning-capable model explicitly — that pin is an agent-level setting on the loop's Hand, resolved like any other (§4.1).
  • Mismatch on sync = re-embed job, never merge (restated from local-models §11); the index's {model_ref, dim} stamp is the guard.
  • Server-side indexes (flint-forge/BossFang corpus): may bind heavier models (BGE-M3 hybrid) and optionally embed in-database via Flint Ember; devices keep a device-appropriate binding over their hot subset. Two indexes, two bindings, one query plan — the read path merges results, it does not pretend the vectors are comparable.

7. Usage-based suggestions

All signals are local-only (SurrealDB; no analytics pipeline — FUNC-SPEC §09), the engine is rules over counters, and every suggestion is a dismissible card that explains itself and applies with one tap — never an automatic switch.

Tracked per (context, model_ref): use counts and recency; measured latency/tok/s; error and malformed-tool-call rates; regenerate-with-a-different-model events (the strongest preference signal: the user tried A, redid it with B); manual override frequency per assistant/topic-class; token spend per cloud provider (priced from the registry) vs. local; provider health history.

The cards these rules produce:

  • "In coding conversations you switch to Qwen3-Coder 8 of the last 10 times — make it the Coding assistant's model?"
  • "Inbox Triage has an 18 % malformed-tool-call rate on Qwen3-4B. Its target home-mac can run 30B-A3B at ~40 t/s — redeploy?" (agent-level, ties §4.1 to the tool-calling floor)
  • "This month: $14.20 to Anthropic for summarization tasks your local utility.fast model handles within quality thresholds — route utility tasks local?"
  • "Provider Groq failed 40 % of requests this week — health-check or disable?"
  • "Phi-4-mini hasn't been used in 90 days — reclaim 2.3 GB?"
  • After a benchmark: "Measured 47 t/s on the new model — 2.1× faster than your current chat default with equal capability tags. Swap?"

Suggestion cards land in the Models tile and (for agent-level ones) on the Hand's detail card, in the moodboard's cyan-annotation style: claim, evidence, one action.

S26-002 · 1. Principles

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

1. Principles

  1. The catalog is signed data, not code (§4). Models, quants, sizes, hashes, licenses, and hardware requirements ship as a versioned manifest the app fetches and verifies — never as constants in the binary.
  2. Recommend, never force. Detection produces a recommendation with a visible reason ("8 GB unified memory → Gemma-3n-2B-Q4"); the library stays open (sideload, override). This is the "library, not a menu" stance from the moodboard.
  3. The first token is the onboarding goal. Everything in §2 is ordered so the user reaches a working first generation as fast as their connection allows, with honest progress and a working app while they wait.
  4. Trust is structural: SHA-256 on every artifact, signed manifests, and a load-and-generate smoke test before a model is marked Active (§7). llama.cpp does not verify integrity at load time — there is an open upstream request for exactly this (ggml-org/llama.cpp#15250) — so verification is our job, in the acquisition layer.
  5. One state machine, three transports. Discovery → fit-check → consent → fetch → verify → activate is identical everywhere; only the fetch adapter differs per tier.

S26-003 · 2. Onboarding (first run)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

2. Onboarding (first run)

The Engine Card is the destination: green dot, model name, live tok/s. First run is the path to lighting it up.

Step 0 — instant utility. The app must be usable before any model lands: UI opens, settings work, and (web/desktop) a "connect to a BossFang instance or cloud provider" escape hatch exists so a user on hotel Wi-Fi isn't staring at a progress bar. If a peer instance is reachable, offer remote inference now while the local model downloads in the background.

Step 1 — probe (silent, <1 s). Run the DeviceProfile probe (§3). No consent needed; nothing leaves the device. Cache in settings; re-probe on hardware change (eGPU, RAM upgrade, browser update enabling WebGPU).

Step 2 — recommend (one card, one number). Show a single recommended model with size, why it was chosen, and what it costs: "Gemma-3n-2B-Q4 · 1.5 GB download · runs ~47 tok/s on this Mac." Secondary link: "choose a different model" opens the full library with fits / tight / won't-fit badges. License display happens here (§5.4): permissive licenses (Apache-2.0/MIT) get a link; restricted-license models get an explicit acceptance step before download.

Step 3 — consent to the download, with the right defaults per tier. - Desktop: start immediately on click; show resumable progress in the Engine Card slot. - Mobile: disclose size prominently; default Wi-Fi only (user can override to cellular); warn on low storage or low battery; the download survives app suspension (§6.3). - Web: check navigator.storage.estimate() against the artifact size first; request navigator.storage.persist(); if the browser lacks WebGPU or refuses persistence, say so plainly and offer the smaller/CPU-lane model or a remote instance instead.

Step 4 — verify + activate (§7), then benchmark. The first activation runs the 30-second micro-benchmark; its measured tok/s becomes the Engine Card number and is stored in the device profile. If decode lands under the usability floor (~8–10 tok/s), offer the next model down with the measurement as the reason.

Step 5 — background upsell, never a blocker. Larger models the hardware can carry ("this machine could run Gemma-4-3B — 2.1 GB") appear as a dismissible suggestion in the Models tile, never as onboarding friction.

Re-onboarding paths reuse the same flow: new device via OFP (peer already has the GGUF → LAN fetch, §5.3), restored backup (models are excluded from backups → re-offer), storage eviction (web/mobile → detect at load, §7, re-offer).

S26-006 · 3.2 The fit test

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

3.2 The fit test

fits :=  weights(quant)
       + kv_cache(ctx_len, n_layers, kv_quant)
       + compute_buffers
       + headroom            <  budget
  • budget = VRAM on discrete GPUs; 60–70 % of unified/system RAM elsewhere (the app, SurrealDB, and the OS live in the same pool — on iOS use the jetsam-derived figure).
  • Choose quant by budget: Q4_K_M default; Q8_0 when abundant; when constrained, drop a model size tier before dropping below Q4 — harsh quants degrade quality faster than smaller models do.
  • Context length is part of the equation: the same model "fits" at 4k and doesn't at 32k. The recommendation pins a default ctx per device tier and says so.

S26-009 · 5. Distribution: Hugging Face vs. a KnowMe-controlled origin

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5. Distribution: Hugging Face vs. a KnowMe-controlled origin

S26-010 · 5.1 The decision

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.1 The decision

Primary: a KnowMe-controlled origin. Hugging Face as fallback. HF tokens only for genuinely gated models the user brings their own account for.

The licensing landscape makes this clean for the entire curated catalog: Qwen and Mistral ship Apache-2.0, Phi ships MIT, and Gemma 4 moved to Apache-2.0 in 2026 (VentureBeat, MindStudio); earlier Gemma generations use the Gemma Terms of Use, which permit redistribution with pass-through of the use restrictions — which is exactly how Ollama serves Gemma from its own registry today (ollama.com license blob). So we can legally mirror everything in the default catalog and control our own availability, latency, and versioning.

Why not HF as primary: HF's gated-model access is granted to individual users, never to organizations — a shared org token cannot download gated repos on users' behalf (HF gated-models docs) — and resolve-URL semantics, rate limits, and repo layout changes are all outside our control. HF remains a listed fallback source for permissive models (anonymous resolve/main/<file> URLs work ungated — HF downloading docs) and the only path for gated models, where the flow is: user pastes their own HF token (stored in OS keychain via Tauri secure storage; per-user, per HF policy — HF token docs).

S26-011 · 5.2 The KnowMe origin, concretely

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.2 The KnowMe origin, concretely

  • Storage/CDN: Cloudflare R2 behind a custom domain (models.know-me.tools) — zero egress fees make multi-GB artifacts economically sane (R2 overview), and a custom-domain public bucket with CDN caching is the recommended pattern for large public artifacts (R2 access patterns, community guidance).
  • Auth model: no authentication for free-catalog artifacts. Integrity comes from the signed manifest + SHA-256, not from access control; anonymous download is a feature (no account required — FUNC-SPEC §09 "no central account"). Range requests work natively, which resumable downloads (§6) depend on.
  • Pro-tier licensed models (the Qwen-35B-class artifacts) are the one place owned auth earns its keep: a license key (issued at purchase, stored in keychain) is exchanged at a tiny token service for a short-lived presigned URL (R2 presigned URLs) or passed to a Cloudflare Worker gate in front of the private bucket (Worker-gated R2 pattern). Keys authorize download, not inference — once fetched and verified, the model runs offline forever, preserving the sovereignty guarantee.
  • Layout: content-addressed, Ollama-style. Store blobs under /blobs/sha256/<digest> with catalog manifests pointing at digests — the OCI-like blob/manifest split Ollama uses is the proven shape for model distribution (Ollama storage internals, DeepWiki: registry & layers). This makes the same blobs trivially publishable to IPFS (same digests → CIDs) and to an OCI registry later, aligning with the .pxt distribution story in the extensibility spec.

S26-012 · 5.3 Source preference order (per artifact, walked by the fetcher)

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

5.3 Source preference order (per artifact, walked by the fetcher)

  1. LAN/OFP peer that already holds the digest (BossFang instance) — free, fast, sovereign;
  2. KnowMe origin (R2/CDN);
  3. IPFS gateway (own gateway first, public fallback) — same digest;
  4. Hugging Face resolve URL (anonymous, or user token if gated).

Every source yields bytes that must hash to the same SHA-256; a source that fails verification is skipped and reported, never trusted.

5.4 License UX

acceptance_required: false (Apache/MIT): show the license link, no click-through. acceptance_required: true (Gemma-Terms-class, Pro licensed models): record {model, license_version, timestamp} locally on acceptance, gate the download on it, and pass the terms through in the UI — that pass-through is what the Gemma terms require of redistributors.

Persistent DownloadTask records in SurrealDB: {model, artifact, source, bytes_total, bytes_done, state} with states queued → fetching → verifying → smoke-testing → ready | failed(reason). S26-017 · 6.3 Mobile — use the OS transfer service, not reqwest

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.3 Mobile — use the OS transfer service, not reqwest

A foreground Rust download dies on suspension. Use URLSession background sessions on iOS (survives suspension and app termination; OS-managed retry; delegate wakes the app on completion — mind the gotchas: background sessions are discretionary under Low Power Mode/poor connectivity, per Apple's forums guidance and field notes) and WorkManager-scheduled DownloadManager on Android (constraint-aware: unmetered network, storage, battery). The FRB bridge only observes: platform code reports progress/completion; Rust verifies the hash and finalizes. Defaults: Wi-Fi-only (overridable), no auto-start on cellular, isExcludedFromBackup = true on iOS (models must not inflate iCloud backups), never bundle weights in the app binary.

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

6.4 Web — delegate to WebLLM, manage the edges

WebLLM fetches shards and caches via the Cache API (or IndexedDB via appConfig.cacheBackend) (docs). KnowMe's appConfig points model URLs at the KnowMe origin (§5.2) rather than HF. Around it: storage.estimate() preflight; storage.persist() request with honest messaging when denied; eviction detection at engine init (cache miss → re-offer); WebGPU absence → offer the wllama/WASM-CPU lane for small models or a remote instance (the dual-lane pattern in webgpu-webllm-app). Safari today means "small models or remote" — say it, don't fake it.

S26-019 · 7. Post-download validation

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

7. Post-download validation

Marking a model Ready requires all five gates, in order:

  1. Hash gate — streaming SHA-256 equals the manifest digest (web: per-shard).
  2. Format gate — parse the GGUF header/metadata (magic, version, tensor count, arch) without full load; catches truncation and wrong-file errors cheaply. GGUF corruption and version drift are the top field failure classes (corruption guide, load-failure taxonomy).
  3. Load gate — actually instantiate on the selected backend with the profile's ctx/offload settings; catches OOM-at-load, backend/driver issues, unsupported quant-arch combos. On failure, retry once on the CPU lane to distinguish "bad file" from "bad backend" and report accordingly.
  4. Smoke gate — one short deterministic generation (fixed prompt, temp 0, ~16 tokens): asserts non-empty, valid UTF-8, no NaN/garbage repetition. Not a quality eval — a "the tensors are sane" check. (This is the layer llama.cpp itself doesn't provide — #15250.)
  5. Benchmark gate (first activation) — the §3.3 micro-benchmark; records measured tok/s; triggers the downgrade suggestion below the usability floor.

Re-validation: gates 1–2 re-run whenever the file's mtime/size changed or after storage eviction events; a Ready model that fails gate 3 at any later launch is demoted to needs-repair with a one-click re-download (blobs are content-addressed, so repair means "fetch the digest again", not "figure out what broke").

11. Embedding models for RAG (all tiers)

The memory/RAG layer (SurrealDB graph + sqlite-vec on mobile, PGlite/pgvector on web/desktop, Postgres+pgvector on flint-forge) needs embeddings everywhere the LLM runs — and unlike chat models, the embedding model must be consistent per index: vectors from different models (or different truncation dims) don't compare. The catalog therefore stamps {embedding_model_id, dim} into every index/KB it creates, and OFP sync treats a mismatch as a re-embed job, not a merge.

Model Size Dims Why / where
EmbeddingGemma-300M — the default everywhere ~300 MB (Q8; <200 MB quantized) 768, Matryoshka-truncatable to 512/256/128 100+ languages, 2k ctx, built for on-device; runs on every tier including midrange Android and the browser (ONNX/transformers.js). Truncate to 256 on mobile (sqlite-vec size/speed), keep 768 on desktop/server — same model, so re-embedding on upgrade is optional, but dims must match within one index
Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B — quality upgrade ~600 MB flexible 32–1024 (MRL) Instruction-aware (task prefixes buy 1–5 %), 100+ languages; the desktop/BossFang default when quality beats footprint

Tiering that falls out: phones and web embed with EmbeddingGemma@256 locally (queries always embeddable offline); desktop embeds with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B@768 or EmbeddingGemma@768; BossFang/flint-forge can maintain a BGE-M3 hybrid index for the heavy corpus and serve it to devices via the read path — devices keep a local EmbeddingGemma index over their own hot subset. Embedding artifacts flow through the same §5 origin, §6 downloader, and §7 gates (smoke test: embed a fixed sentence, assert dim + finite norm + cosine-similarity sanity against a stored reference vector). S30-001 · UAR knowledge base, RAG, and Karpathy wiki strategy

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

UAR knowledge base, RAG, and Karpathy wiki strategy

Status: architecture assessment Date: 2026-07-19 Scope: knowledge architecture and delivery strategy only; no runtime code is implemented by this document KBD phase context: model-runtime-per-device; implementation is 4 of 5 after completing this document-only change

S30-002 · Decision

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Decision

Use the Universal Agent Runtime (UAR) as the shared knowledge control plane, but deploy a different runtime profile at each platform boundary:

  • Mobile: embed a small, platform-safe UAR knowledge kernel in the shared Rust core. Flutter reaches it only through typed FFI. Reuse KnowMe's existing embedded SurrealDB hybrid graph store rather than creating a second mobile database or vector index.
  • Desktop: run exactly one supervised UAR service. BossFang supervises it when BossFang is present; KnowMe supervises it otherwise. Both clients may use the service, but they must not start competing UAR writers for the same scope.
  • Web: run UAR as a private service behind the KnowMe Axum application. React communicates with the Axum boundary, not directly with UAR and never with provider credentials.

The knowledge system has three related but deliberately separate artifact classes:

  1. Evidence corpus: source documents, chunks, embeddings, lexical indexes, graph facts, and citations used by RAG.
  2. Karpathy wiki: concise, human-readable Markdown lessons distilled from evidence and evaluated execution traces.
  3. Episodic memory: run events, tool outcomes, feedback, checkpoints, and evaluation records from which lessons may be proposed.

Raw evidence, wiki revisions, provenance, and tombstones are canonical and syncable. Embeddings, BM25 indexes, graph projections, and retrieval caches are derived per device and rebuilt against a declared model binding. Vector rows must not be merged across different embedding models or dimensions.

S30-004 · Evidence language and source snapshot

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Evidence language and source snapshot

This document uses the following status language deliberately:

  • Observed: directly verified in repository source or an official source.
  • Inference: a conclusion drawn from multiple observed facts; the inference is identified as such.
  • Decision/recommendation: the architecture this strategy selects; it is not a claim that implementation already exists.
  • Blocker: missing evidence or capability that prevents certification.
  • Open decision: a product, legal, policy, or ownership choice that this architecture cannot safely infer.
  • Future stage: ordered work proposed by this strategy, not work completed by this document.

Local implementation observations were rechecked against UAR commit 9bee88d9745f82d7a63445c36e5e4c6a42048fd5 and the concurrent KnowMe working tree on 2026-07-19. Later submodule revisions require revalidation before these status claims are reused.

The original RAG work treats retrieval as explicit non-parametric memory that improves updateability and provenance, while the Ragas framework separates retrieval quality from answer faithfulness and relevance. That distinction maps cleanly to UAR's knowledge APIs and to a separate, reviewable wiki layer. Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Es et al., Ragas provide the research basis.

The codebase already contains most of the seams needed for this direction:

  • UAR has knowledge-base CRUD, ingestion and search APIs, embedding backends, citation events, a retrieval pipeline abstraction, lexical verification, and hybrid vector/graph RRF.
  • The UAR submodule includes prometheus-knowledge: a Markdown wiki, TF-IDF focus/search, linting, a trace store, evaluation, trace-to-wiki compilation, MCP tools, and a UAR tool-provider bridge.
  • KnowMe already has an embedded SurrealDB graph store with 384-dimensional embeddings, BM25, vector search, graph expansion, and RRF.
  • KnowMe already projects UAR run events into its UI protocol, but mobile UAR execution is explicitly reported as not wired.

Those are useful foundations, not proof of production readiness. The current UAR Rust SDK's embedded builder still starts the full HTTP server and does not expose populated direct-runtime handles. Its root crate is monolithic and its smallest published bundle still includes the Surreal backend. The product matrix marks web stable, desktop preview, mobile experimental, and arbitrary browser WASM unsupported. The present self-learning CLI also has concrete gaps: Codex/OpenCode file adapters return no trace data, trace fields are incompletely correlated, and the CLI's compile block does not yet invoke the available batch compiler.

S30-006 · Artifact and authority model

Governing revision: CX-01–08 · source requirement, not release evidence.

Artifact and authority model

Artifact Purpose Canonical form Derived form Default authority
Source document Verifiable evidence Original bytes or normalized text plus content hash Chunks and extracted metadata Ingesting knowledge scope
Chunk Retrieval unit Text span with source offsets and lineage Embedding and lexical postings Corpus revision
Graph fact Multi-hop/entity context Typed relation with supporting source spans Neighborhood/community summaries Corpus revision
Wiki entry Reusable lesson or anti-pattern Markdown with revision, tags, claims, provenance, confidence TF-IDF/vector representation Project-private by default
Execution trace Learning evidence Redacted structured run/tool/outcome record Evaluation features and aggregates Session/project scope
Evaluation Promotion evidence Metric results, grader version, golden-set version Dashboard projections Evaluation run
Skill revision Executable behavior Versioned skill artifact and policy decision Runtime caches Human-approved release

The evidence corpus answers “what sources support this response?” The wiki answers “what durable lesson has survived evaluation?” Episodic memory answers “what happened during this run?” Conflating them would make retention, trust, and conflict handling unmanageable.

Every record should carry, as applicable:

  • tenant, user, workspace/project, knowledge-base, agent, run, and session scopes;
  • source URI or local source identity, content hash, capture time, and parser version;
  • embedding model identifier, immutable revision, dimension, normalization, and chunking policy;
  • origin device/runtime, creation actor, sensitivity class, consent basis, and retention class;
  • parent revision, supersedes relation, tombstone state, and synchronization clock;
  • claim-to-source spans for wiki entries and answer citations.

The safe default is project-private and user-private. Cross-project or shared-global knowledge is an explicit promotion, never an inference from filesystem location or account identity.
